title: Stalks of tilde modules are localizations
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $\mathfrak p\subset R$ a prime ideal with point $x\in X$, and $S=R\setminus\mathfrak p$. Let $S\subseteq R$ be a multiplicative subset of a commutative ring $R$. An $R$-linear map $\ell:P\to P'$ of $R$-modules is a *localization of $P$ at $S$* if (a) every $s\in S$ acts bijectively on $P'$, (b) every element of $P'$ is $s^{-1}\ell(p)$ for some $p\in P$, $s\in S$, and (c) $\ell(p)=\ell(q)$ implies $sp=sq$ for some $s\in S$ (equivalently, (a) holds and $S^{-1}P\to P'$, $p/s\mapsto s^{-1}\ell(p)$, is bijective). Let $\rho:R=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ be the germ map, which is a localization of $R$ at $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field]. For an $R$-module $M$ let $\widetilde M$ and $\tau_X:M\to\widetilde M(X)$ be as in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], and regard the stalk $\widetilde M_x$, an $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], as an $R$-module via $\rho$. Then the map $\lambda_M:M\to\widetilde M_x$, $m\mapsto\tau_X(m)_x$ (the germ at $x$), is $R$-linear and is a localization of $M$ at $S$; so $\widetilde M_x\cong M_{\mathfrak p}$, $\tau_X(m)_x\leftrightarrow m/1$, as modules over $\mathcal O_{X,x}\cong R_{\mathfrak p}$.
